newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel falls on Thomson sale talk.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel falls on Thomson sale talk.

text.p: Shares in French engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom fell late on Tuesday on market talk that the government had picked Alcatel's bid for the Thomson SA electronics group, traders said.

The rumour was that the government would announce Alcatel as the winner on Tuesday evening but that the missiles activity would be sold to Lagardere, depriving Alcatel of that blue-chip business, one operator said.
Alcatel closed down 2.22 percent at 444.90 francs, while Lagardere was up 2.94 percent at 133.10 francs.
Lagardere, Alcatel and Thomson officials declined comment.

Finance minister Jean Arthuis earlier told the National Assembly that a decision on the Thomson privatisation would be made in the "coming days" and the state's preferred bidder would be referred to the Privatisation Commission.
It was unclear whether the government would name its choice before the Privatisation Commission had studies it.
The market has been expecting a decision this week on the Thomson sale, with the betting heavily in favour of Alcatel.
Thomson is being sold off as part of the government's reorganisation of the defence industry.
